# Robustness {#sec-robustness}

The pre-registration fixed the robustness rows before any confirmatory result was seen (PAP §8.2), and every row was run. This section says what the rows vary, how they are reported, and which rows move each confirmatory estimate furthest. @fig-robustness-rq1 places the RQ1 rows beside the primary coefficients, @fig-robustness-market does the same for H5 and H5b, and each row's full record is in Appendix D (@sec-app-robustness-tables).

## What the rows vary

The rows fall into six groups. Construction rows change how the exposure measure is built: the following OEWS vintage of employment weights ({{< var vintage.oews.r1 >}}, R1, labelled look-ahead for H5 and H5b), wage-bill weights (R2), dropping occupations without AEI usage instead of assigning them zero (R3, the D3 assumption of @sec-data), the API source for Design `A_pooled` (R4), the suppression bounds in place of the point measure (R10), employment-weighted task allocation (R11), standardised ranks (R12), the AIOE crosswalk (R14), the headquarters industry redistributed (R15), the r6 task-allocated basis (R16), the GPT-4 Eloundou β (R17), the majority crosswalk mode (R20), other indices in place of `z_delegation` (R21), strict real-time inputs (R32) and the employment-weighted NAICS-to-SIC crosswalk (R33). Sample rows change which industries or days enter: FF30 and FF48 granularity (R6), dropping Hardw, Softw and Chips (R7), excluding the large-cap rally year in Design A (R8), placebo event dates (R9) and dropping Softw (R13). The returns row uses equal-weighted industry returns (R5). Inference rows change the null scale or the statistic: non-overlapping windows (R18), the root mean square around the null value (R19), earlier-starting windows (R34), the studentised statistic (R35) and one-way occupation clustering (R38). RQ1 rows vary the behavioural hypotheses (R22 to R28, R31, R36 and R37), and the H6 rows vary the filing sample and the dictionary (R29, R30).

## Reporting rules

The rules are those of PAP §8.1, fixed in `{{< var pap.tag >}}`. Every row is reported whatever its result, and the summary table of Appendix D (@sec-app-robustness-tables) sets each row's estimate beside the primary's. No row changes a confirmatory decision; the one exception is R13, a pre-registered co-condition of the H5 and H5b claim (@sec-markets). No row carries error control across rows, R21 among them, and the rows are not summarised by tallying their results. RQ1 rows use the inference of the hypothesis they vary (@sec-methods). Market rows recompute the null scale s, the null value b̄ and the critical for the row's exposure vector or sample by the same pre-seal procedure, over the same {{< var power.n_windows >}} historical windows with the t₂₁ rule and the D21 null. Every robustness market interval in this paper, for H5, H5b and the H6 gap–return slope, is the interval b̂ ± c·s with c the critical at level {{< var design.alpha.h5_second >}}, recomputed for the row (R35 uses its own scale and t₂₁ critical); the row files do not print the interval at the first Holm level, {{< var design.alpha.h5_first >}}. Any statement that a market robustness result is not rejected takes the fixed P14 form of the H5 and H5b wording in @sec-markets, with its interval and its MDE; no MDE is computed for an individual row, so this section reports estimates, intervals and p and makes no such statement.

## RQ1

For H1 the primary coefficients are β_e = {{< var rq1.h1.beta_e >}} pp of automation per year of education and β_w = {{< var rq1.h1.beta_w >}} pp per unit of log wage, and H1 is {{< var rq1.h1.decision_text >}}: the null that β_e or β_w is zero is not rejected at {{< var rq1.holm.h1 >}} (@sec-rq1). R24 r5 is the one robustness row under which the H1 p-value, {{< var rob.r24.r5.p_h1.p >}}, falls below that level with both coefficients negative (β_e = {{< var rob.r24.r5.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r24.r5.log_wage.estimate >}}); it is a pre-registered robustness row and changes no decision. The other rows that move the H1 coefficients furthest are R24 r4, where β_w changes sign to {{< var rob.r24.r4.log_wage.estimate >}}; R24 `r6_1p_api` (β_e = {{< var rob.r24.r6_1p_api.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r24.r6_1p_api.log_wage.estimate >}}); R26 with GWA fixed effects (β_e = {{< var rob.r26.gwa.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r26.gwa.log_wage.estimate >}}) and with DWA fixed effects (β_e = {{< var rob.r26.dwa.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r26.dwa.log_wage.estimate >}}); and R10 at the upper bound (β_e = {{< var rob.r10.h1_ub.human_education_years_mean.estimate >}}, β_w = {{< var rob.r10.h1_ub.log_wage.estimate >}}).

For H2 the primary trend is β = {{< var rq1.h2.beta >}} pp per year, and H2 is {{< var rq1.h2.decision_text >}}: the release-level co-condition fails. The measured rise is one r2-to-r3 step followed by a fall, leaving out r2 reverses the sign of β ({{< var diag.h2.leave_out_release_r2.beta >}}), and that step coincides with a change of the classified-conversation base, so classifier or platform drift cannot be separated from behaviour (@sec-rq1). The rows that run the other way are R22 on the API source over r3 to r5 ({{< var rob.r22.api_r3_r5.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r22.api_r3_r5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r22.api_r3_r5.ci_hi >}}]) and R23 with `ai_autonomy_mean` ({{< var rob.r23.h2.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r23.h2.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r23.h2.ci_hi >}}]). In the same direction as the primary lie R22's all-releases series ({{< var rob.r22.all_r2_r6.estimate >}}), labelled confounded with the r6 suppression-regime change, R22's unbalanced panel ({{< var rob.r22.unbalanced.estimate >}}) and R36 with publication dates ({{< var rob.r36.h2.estimate >}}); R37, descriptive, gives a within-r6 change of {{< var rob.r37.h2.estimate >}}.

For H3 the primary is γ = {{< var rq1.h3.gamma >}} pp of validation share, and H3 is {{< var rq1.h3.decision_text >}}: the null that γ is zero is not rejected at {{< var rq1.holm.h3 >}}. No generated file ranks the H3 rows, so they are reported unordered: R10 at the upper bound gives {{< var rob.r10.h3_ub.estimate >}} (interval [{{< var rob.r10.h3_ub.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r10.h3_ub.ci_hi >}}]); R27, with the continuous Consequence of Error, gives {{< var rob.r27.h3.estimate >}} pp per standard deviation; R31, adding H1's covariates, gives {{< var rob.r31.error_cost.estimate >}}; and R38 gives {{< var rob.r38.h3.estimate >}} (p = {{< var rob.r38.h3.p >}}).

For H4 the primary coefficients are b₁ = {{< var rq1.h4.b1 >}} pp per unit of log AUI and b₂ = {{< var rq1.h4.b2 >}} pp per unit of log GDP per working-age person, and H4 is {{< var rq1.h4.decision_text >}} (@sec-rq1). Nor are the H4 rows ranked. R25 tests the coefficients separately in a five-member Holm family: p = {{< var rob.r25.h4a.p >}} for b₁ and p = {{< var rob.r25.h4b.p >}} for b₂. R28 uses other units and weights: US states (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.us_states.log_aui.estimate >}}, b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.us_states.log_income.estimate >}}), r4 countries (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.r4_countries.log_aui.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r28.r4_countries.log_aui.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r28.r4_countries.log_aui.ci_hi >}}]; b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.r4_countries.log_income.estimate >}}), r5 countries (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.r5_countries.log_aui.estimate >}}, b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.r5_countries.log_income.estimate >}}), usage weights (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.usage_weighted.log_aui.estimate >}}, b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.usage_weighted.log_income.estimate >}}) and the IWA-level mix (b₁ = {{< var rob.r28.iwa_mix.log_aui.estimate >}}, b₂ = {{< var rob.r28.iwa_mix.log_income.estimate >}}).

## Market rows

For H5 the primary is b̂ = {{< var rq3.h5.b_pp2 >}} pp of annualised alpha per standard deviation of exposure, and H5 is {{< var rq3.h5.decision_text >}}, in the fixed wording of @sec-markets. The rows that move b̂ furthest are R7, dropping Hardw, Softw and Chips ({{< var rob.r07.h5.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r07.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r07.h5.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r07.h5.p >}}); R12, standardised ranks ({{< var rq3.h5_r12.b >}}); and R5, equal-weighted returns ({{< var rob.r05.h5.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r05.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r05.h5.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r05.h5.p >}}). For H5b the primary is b̂ = {{< var rq3.h5b.b_pp2 >}}, and H5b is {{< var rq3.h5b.decision_text >}}. The rows that move it furthest are R12 ({{< var rq3.h5b_r12.b >}}), R7 ({{< var rob.r07.h5b.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r07.h5b.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r07.h5b.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r07.h5b.p >}}) and R6 at FF30 ({{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r06.h5b.ff30.p >}}).

Every H5 and H5b number carries the S1 timing caveat of @sec-data. Design B's {{< var vintage.oews.primary >}} OEWS weights were released on {{< var design.s1.oews_release >}}, after the {{< var design.formation >}} formation date and inside the return window, and the O\*NET {{< var vintage.onet.primary >}} links postdate formation, although its task text is identical to that of {{< var vintage.onet.r32 >}}. Design B is out of sample in AEI data only, not strictly real-time. R32, the strict real-time row ({{< var vintage.oews.r32 >}} weights), gives {{< var rob.r32.h5.estimate >}} for H5 (interval [{{< var rob.r32.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r32.h5.ci_hi >}}]) and {{< var rob.r32.h5b.estimate >}} for H5b (interval [{{< var rob.r32.h5b.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r32.h5b.ci_hi >}}]); R1, labelled look-ahead, gives {{< var rob.r01.h5.estimate >}} and {{< var rob.r01.h5b.estimate >}}.

## H6

H6 is exploratory throughout (@sec-markets). Its divergence Spearman is ρ = {{< var h6.spearman.rho >}} (interval [{{< var h6.spearman.ci.lo >}}, {{< var h6.spearman.ci.hi >}}]). Two inputs are fixed at retrieval ({{< var h6.vintage.submissions_retrieved_utc >}}), not at the filing year: each filer's FF49 industry is its current SIC from the EDGAR submissions file, and the numerator uses the SEC full-text search's phrase matching on the retrieval date. The R29 parts whose intervals cover zero are the change in talk ({{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.change_2019_2024.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.change_2019_2024.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.change_2019_2024.ci_hi >}}]), the float-weighted filers ({{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.float_weighted.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.float_weighted.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.float_weighted.ci_hi >}}]) and the pre-formation filings ({{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.pre_formation_2025.estimate >}}, interval [{{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.pre_formation_2025.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_divergence.pre_formation_2025.ci_hi >}}]). R30's narrow and broad dictionaries give {{< var rob.r30.h6_divergence.narrow.estimate >}} and {{< var rob.r30.h6_divergence.broad.estimate >}}. The exploratory gap–return slope is {{< var h6.gap_returns.b >}} pp per standard deviation of the gap in the primary and {{< var rob.r29.h6_gap_return.change_2019_2024.estimate >}} under the change in talk (interval [{{< var rob.r29.h6_gap_return.change_2019_2024.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r29.h6_gap_return.change_2019_2024.ci_hi >}}]); no MDE computed (exploratory).

## Where the rows are

Appendix D (@sec-app-robustness-tables) prints each row file unedited, the summary table, and the table of implementation choices where the PAP is silent, each with the §11 clarification it names. It also records the reproduction tolerance that PAP §11 fixes for the row files (C-80): a re-run reproduces every row file byte for byte, and a regenerated CSV is accepted when its non-numeric cells are identical and its numeric cells agree within a fixed relative tolerance.
